title: Upper tail of the positive-coordinate count
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, and choose a point uniformly from the $n$-dimensional sign cube. The probability that its number of positive coordinates exceeds $\left\lfloor \frac n2+\frac n2\sqrt{\frac{2\log(48n)}{n}}\right\rfloor$ is at most $\frac{1}{24n}$.
